key_insight: In a young-onset neuropsychiatry cohort, Alzheimer’s and psychiatric polygenic risk scores showed distinct disease associations, with no detected associations with plasma biomarkers.
clinical_relevance: Genetic risk and plasma biomarkers may capture different information, but their combined diagnostic value remains unproven.
method: Studied 687 European-ancestry participants: 195 controls, 283 with primary psychiatric disorders, 55 with Alzheimer’s disease and 154 with other neurodegenerative diseases.
Computed five polygenic risk scores excluding APOE; adjusted models for age, sex and APOE ε4 dose.
Evaluated plasma NfL, GFAP and p-tau217 in 332 participants.
evidence_signal: Alzheimer’s and psychiatric risk scores were associated with their corresponding diagnoses versus controls (OR per SD 1.69 and 1.29, respectively); adding Alzheimer’s genetic risk to NfL yielded little change in psychiatric-versus-other-neurodegenerative discrimination (AUC 0.764 to 0.773).
watch_item: The European-ancestry sample and small Alzheimer’s subgroup limit generalizability; larger longitudinal cohorts are needed before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Alzheimers disease and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers in a real-world young-onset dementia cohort.
